title: They trusted Egypt… and God made their illusion walk barefoot.
paragraphs: They trusted Egypt… and God made their illusion walk barefoot.

No armor.
No sandals.
No dignity left to hide behind.

And somehow—
that was the message.

Because what they trusted…
was about to collapse.
You don’t feel it at first.

The subtle shift from “God is my refuge”
to “God… plus this.”

This job.
This relationship.
This hidden sin that “helps you cope.”
This image you protect more than your soul.

But deep down—
you’ve built a backup savior.
They still had temple language, religious rhythm, sacred songs.
Isaiah walked barefoot for three years.

No sandals.
Stripped down.
Public.
Uncomfortable.
Humiliating.
A prophet turned into a living warning.
Because Judah was trusting a nation that would soon be led away naked and ashamed.
“You’re leaning on something that cannot stand.”
Here’s the part we don’t like.

God will sometimes let your false security break—
not to destroy you…

That moment when the relationship ends.
That moment when the money dries up.
That moment when your reputation cracks.

Isaiah 20:3–4 (ESV):
“Then the Lord said, ‘As my servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and a portent against Egypt and Cush, so shall the king of Assyria lead away the Egyptian captives… naked and barefoot, with buttocks uncovered, the nakedness of Egypt.’”
Because God is not interested in protecting illusions.
He is interested in saving souls.
Some scholars interpret this passage as a prophetic act meant to shock Judah out of spiritual complacency. Others see it as a direct visual prophecy of Egypt’s coming humiliation under Assyria.
What you trust apart from God will eventually fail you publicly.
It’s not just that your “Egypt” will fail…
It’s that your heart was never meant to be held by it.
This is where the story turns.
Because Isaiah didn’t just point to judgment.

Who would also be stripped.
Exposed.
Publicly shamed.
But not for His own sin.

Matthew 27:28 (ESV):
“And they stripped him and put a scarlet robe on him.”

Where Isaiah signaled judgment…
Jesus absorbed it.

Where Isaiah exposed false trust…
Jesus became the only true refuge.
your misplaced trust, your hidden sin, your quiet idolatries—

2 Corinthians 5:21 (ESV):
“For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.”
The nakedness of Isaiah was a warning.
The nakedness of Christ was a rescue.
It’s not the end of your story.

It’s the mercy of God pulling you away from a collapsing lie
and leading you into unshakable truth.
You don’t need a backup savior.
What are you still leaning on?
What are you secretly trusting more than God?
What would leave you exposed if it disappeared tomorrow?
Turn your heart fully back to Christ.

Not halfway.
Not “God plus something.”
Not divided loyalty.
Because the safest place you can be…

Psalm 20:7 (ESV):
“Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we trust in the name of the Lord our God.”
